entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of a One-Sided Exponential
entries.core_move: Compute the continuous-time Fourier transform of a decaying one-sided exponential e^(-a t)$u(t)$ by applying the transform definition over its step-limited support and identifying the basic pair e^(-a t)$u(t) <-> 1/(a + j \omega) for a > 0$.

entries.lesson_title: Real and Imaginary Parts of an Exponential Transform
entries.core_move: Decompose the exponential transform 1/(a + j $\omega$) into its real part a/($a^2$ + $\omega$^2) and imaginary part -$\omega$/($a^2$ + $\omega$^2) by multiplying by the complex conjugate.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of a Rectangular Pulse
entries.core_move: Compute the continuous-time Fourier transform of a finite rectangular pulse by evaluating the transform integral over the pulse interval and converting the result into a scaled sinc spectrum with the correct amplitude, width, and phase.
Interpret the rectangular pulse transform as a sinc-shaped spectrum by identifying how pulse duration and amplitude determine the central lobe, sidelobe oscillations, and frequency-domain scaling.

entries.lesson_title: Zeros of the Rectangular Pulse Spectrum
entries.core_move: Compute the nonzero angular-frequency zeros of a rectangular pulse spectrum by solving sin($\omega$ T/2) = 0 and relating the null spacing to the pulse width T.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of a Time-Domain Impulse
entries.core_move: Compute the continuous-time Fourier transform of a scaled or shifted time-domain impulse by applying the sifting property to obtain the corresponding flat spectrum or complex phase factor.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of a Constant Signal
entries.core_move: Convert a constant signal $x(t) = A into the transform pair X(j \omega) = 2 pi A \delta(\omega) by recognizing constant time-domain content as a frequency-domain impulse at zero frequency$.

entries.lesson_title: Fourier Transform of a Complex Exponential
entries.core_move: Convert e^(j $\omega$_0 t) into the transform pair $X(j \omega) = 2 pi \delta(\omega - omega_0) by recognizing it as a single frequency component shifted away from zero frequency$.

Compute the continuous-time Fourier transform of a cosine by rewriting it as half the sum of opposite-frequency complex exponentials and converting those exponentials into impulses at the positive and negative cosine frequencies.
